title: Your Ebook Title Goes Here
subtitle: One clear, benefit-driven sentence. What will the reader be able to do after reading this? Be specific with a number, timeframe, or quantified outcome.

chapters.title: Chapter One Title
chapters.dreamOutcome: After this chapter, your reader will be able to [do specific thing] in [timeframe] for under [amount]. Write the transformation in one sentence.

sections.label: Hook — Dream Outcome First
sections.heading: What You Will Have After This Chapter
sections.body: Write 3–5 sentences that open with the specific, desirable result the reader gets from this chapter. Lead with the transformation, not the topic. Example: "By the end of this chapter, you'll know exactly how to do X in under Y hours for under $Z — without needing to Z1 or Z2." Make the reader feel the outcome before you teach it.

sections.label: Problem — Name the Pain Precisely
sections.heading: The Real Problem Most People Are Ignoring
sections.body: Write 3–5 sentences naming the specific frustration. Use "Most people who [audience descriptor] struggle with [specific pain]." Be precise — the more specific the pain, the more the reader feels seen. End with: "Here's what actually works."

callout.label: Key Stat or Proof Point
callout.text: Add a supporting statistic, study, or fact here that validates the problem. E.g. "According to [credible source], X% of [audience] experience [problem]." Specificity = credibility.

sections.label: Mechanism — The How
sections.heading: The Step-by-Step Framework
sections.body: This is your core content — the actual value. Write it as numbered steps, a named framework, or a principle-by-principle guide. Be specific: exact prices, named brands, real measurements. Vague advice is cheap; specific guidance is what gets shared and recommended.

sections.label: Proof — Real Example With Numbers
sections.heading: What This Looks Like in the Real World
sections.body: Tell one specific story from your own experience or a reader's. Use the Before → After structure. Include real numbers: cost, time, specific result. One detailed story with numbers beats ten vague testimonials. "In my [specific apartment/home/situation], I did X. Cost: $Y. Time: Z hours. Result: [specific outcome]."

sections.label: Quick Wins — Reduce Perceived Effort
sections.heading: Three Things You Can Do Today
sections.body: List 3–5 immediate actions the reader can take right now, today, with what they already have. Low effort, visible impact. This section makes readers feel the guide is already paying for itself before they finish the chapter.
checklist: Quick win #1 — one sentence, achievable in under 30 minutes
Quick win #2 — one sentence, achievable in under 30 minutes
Quick win #3 — one sentence, achievable in under 30 minutes

sections.label: Takeaway — Bridge Forward
sections.heading: The One Thing to Remember
sections.body: Write one sentence that distils the entire chapter into its core principle. Then one sentence bridging to the next chapter: "Now that you know [this chapter's principle], the next step is [next chapter's topic] — because [reason they're connected]."

chapters.dreamOutcome: After this final chapter, your reader holds a complete, actionable plan. The guide is done. The result is within reach. Now they need to act.

sections.body: [End with conviction. Tell them the single most important principle from the entire guide — the one idea they should take away above all others. Make it memorable, specific, and true. This is what they'll share with others.]

callout.label: Your Call to Action
callout.text: Direct the reader to the next step: visit your website, follow your newsletter, buy the next guide, leave a review, or share with someone who needs this. Make it one clear action, not three. The final CTA is a gift — don't waste it on multiple options.
